subject.title: fix(plugins): rebuild unverifiable managed npm installs

question: When a managed plugin tree exists but its registry integrity cannot be verified, should a failed clean rebuild leave the plugin disabled while retaining the old tree only in quarantine?
rationale: The code can implement either policy correctly, but choosing between fail-closed integrity enforcement and availability-preserving rollback determines the product's trust boundary and upgrade behavior for existing installations.

options.title: Approve fail-closed quarantine
options.body: Accept the patch's policy that unverifiable code is never automatically reactivated, even when the clean rebuild fails, and rely on the reported quarantine path for inspection and recovery.

options.title: Require guided recovery first
options.body: Keep fail-closed quarantine but add a tested error or Doctor recovery flow that lets operators retry or deliberately resolve the quarantined installation before merging.

options.title: Preserve availability rollback
options.body: Restore the prior tree after rebuild failure, explicitly accepting continued execution of code whose registry integrity cannot be established.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed quarantine
recommendation.body: Accept the patch's policy that unverifiable code is never automatically reactivated, even when the clean rebuild fails, and rely on the reported quarantine path for inspection and recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows merge involvement in both the package-lock integrity resolver and adjacent managed npm trust-boundary hardening.
